what_happened: The job "Write landing intent and landing records in land --pr, with push" (20261024-115052-bzw6) failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 3 of 3 the critic still said the plan needed revising. The code references held and the design was sound: build the commit on the remote tip, push with a lease, and move the local ref only after the push succeeds. The one major gap was criterion 8. The plan wrongly said Athena::land_pr cannot run against a fake host, but it takes a `runner: &dyn Runner`. Every records test calls the free gh::land_pr, so the production wiring in Athena::land_pr (which PrLander and drain.rs use) is never exercised. Passing `records: None` there would leave all tests green. Three minor findings were also listed: display.rs is not among the reading's deliverables; a stale merge-requested marker can block merge retries and nothing clears it; and the exit code for a report with warnings is not stated. The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks. Nothing was delivered.
cause: The planning stage asserts what the code can and cannot do in tests without checking it, and it does not require each criterion's demonstration to go through the production entry point. Here the plan claimed a function could not run against a fake host, when it takes an injectable runner. It then tested only the inner function, so the real wiring went unproven. Nothing in the plan template makes the planner name, per criterion, the entry point the demonstration calls and the seam it uses, and confirm the seam exists. The critic finds this only by reading code, so it surfaces late. The three-round cap has no fallback: major findings are not required to shrink, no partial plan is kept, and a retry starts without the earlier critic's findings. This is the same late-critic weakness behind the previous planning failures, including the immediately preceding attempt at this same feature.
prevention: Change the planning stage in three ways. (1) The plan template requires, for each criterion's demonstration, the production entry point called, the fake or seam used, and a check that the seam exists in the code (or the step that adds it). Any claim that something cannot be tested must cite the code. A demonstration that bypasses the production caller must be flagged. (2) The critic's findings from earlier attempts and rounds are carried into the next round and into any retry of the same request. Round 3 must show fewer major findings than round 2, and the plan is kept as a partial plan for operator guidance if it still fails. (3) Add a wiring check: when a plan adds an optional or injected dependency, there must be a demonstration that fails if the production caller passes none.
proposed_request: Change Athena's planning stage so plans cannot assert a test seam without checking it. (1) The plan template must require, for every acceptance criterion, a demonstration that names the production entry point it calls, the fake or injection point it uses, and where in the code that seam exists (or which step adds it). A claim that a function cannot be tested against a fake must cite the code that shows it. (2) When a plan adds an optional or injected dependency (such as a records writer), it must include a demonstration that fails if the production caller passes none. (3) The critic must check these items against the code. (4) The critic's findings from earlier rounds and from earlier failed attempts of the same request must be given to the planner, and a plan that fails after the last round must be kept for the operator. Acceptance: a planning run for a request like "write landing records in land --pr" is rejected by the critic in round 1 if its demonstrations only call the inner function and never Athena::land_pr; and a retry shows the earlier findings in the planner's input.
